reference: procps-ng pidof supplies independent no-match CLI comparisons; positive matching, ordering and root filtering require controlled process records. Bash type/help cases are metadata only.
coverage: Bash type metadata reports pidof as a builtin.
Bash help resolves the pidof help topic and emits metadata.
Deferred: exact comm-versus-argv distinctions and multiple matches; no-match status executes.
Deferred: slash-containing argv[0] basenames; a bare argv[0] match executes.
Deferred: first-match selection across multiple matches; single-child -s/-q execute.
Deferred: interpreter script argv[1] matching with -x.
Deferred: %PPID and multi-ID omission spellings; one numeric child omission executes.
Deferred: differing process roots and multiple-PID custom separators.
Executed no-match lookups and a controlled owned-child argv[0] match with -s/-q and numeric omission.
exclusions: The single owned-child argv[0] lookup and no-match modes execute. Multiple-match enumeration, script/comm distinctions, parent relationships and differing process roots need the additional controlled fixtures described below.
Thread selection, namespace-specific process selection, races during procfs traversal, and non-procps pidof variants are outside this small suite.

cases.purpose: Check Bash type metadata identifies the packaged pidof loadable as a builtin.
Check Bash help resolves pidof metadata and produces a nonempty help entry.
Compare exact-name comm matching, reporting multiple matching processes, and the no-match status/output contract.
cases.reason: Requires a future disposable VM with a private PID namespace and controlled fixture processes whose comm names and PIDs are known, or a reviewed procfs adapter supplying deterministic /proc/PID/comm and cmdline records to both sides. Run procps-ng pidof and bash-os against the same fixture. The current runner gives reference and candidate separate changing process trees, exposes only read-only live procfs, and pidof.c hardcodes /proc.

cases.purpose: Compare argv[0] matching when comm differs, including a command argument containing a directory prefix whose basename should match.
cases.reason: Requires a future disposable VM or reviewed shared procfs mock with NUL-delimited /proc/PID/cmdline records where argv[0] differs from comm, including both bare and slash-containing command arguments. procps-ng pidof must see the same fixed records; the current runner cannot inject them and the candidate opens hardcoded /proc paths.

cases.purpose: Compare -s first-match behavior and -q output suppression while retaining success and no-match statuses.
cases.reason: Requires a future disposable VM with at least two controlled matching processes, or a reviewed procfs mock with stable PID records and enumeration order, plus procps-ng pidof as the reference. The current live /proc snapshot is not shared or pinned between executions, so exact first-match output cannot be checked safely here.

cases.purpose: Compare whether -x includes a script name found as argv[1] of an interpreter, while the default mode excludes that argv[1] match.
cases.reason: Requires a future disposable VM or reviewed procfs mock containing a controlled interpreter cmdline with a NUL-delimited script argv[1], plus the corresponding procps-ng pidof comparison. The current runner provides no stable synthetic cmdline records and the candidate reads hardcoded /proc/PID/cmdline.

cases.purpose: Compare -o omission of numeric PIDs and %PPID, including the documented comma, semicolon, and colon list separators.
cases.reason: Requires a future disposable VM with fixed matching PIDs and a controlled parent relationship, or a reviewed procfs/process-ID mock that gives both procps-ng pidof and the candidate identical process records. The current runner's parent PIDs differ between reference and candidate runs, and the candidate has no injectable proc root.

cases.purpose: Compare -c filtering when one controlled process has the caller's root and another has a different root.
cases.reason: Requires a future disposable VM with controlled process root links or a reviewed procfs mock supplying distinct /proc/PID/root link targets to both implementations. The current runner gives processes one sandbox root and the candidate hardcodes /proc, so the root-filter behavior cannot be isolated with a stable oracle here.

cases.purpose: Compare -S and its -d alias for joining multiple matched PIDs with a requested separator.
cases.reason: Requires a future disposable VM with multiple controlled matching processes or a reviewed shared procfs mock fixing the matched PID set and output order, plus procps-ng pidof for comparison. Separate runner process trees and a live changing /proc prevent deterministic output comparison here.

Match one bounded fixture child by its explicit argv[0], compare its exact PID with Bash $!, and check -s/-q/-o. FIFO handshakes control lifetime; releasing and waiting for the child uses no signals. Dynamic PID identity is asserted locally, not discarded.
cases.script:
mkfifo ready gate
(PATH=/usr/bin:/bin; exec -a parity_pid_fixture_73d9e26b bash --noprofile --norc -c 'printf "ready\n" > ready; IFS= read -r release < gate') &
child=$!
IFS= read -r handshake < ready
if out=$(pidof parity_pid_fixture_73d9e26b); then found=0; else found=$?; fi
if one=$(pidof -s parity_pid_fixture_73d9e26b); then single=0; else single=$?; fi
if quiet=$(pidof -q parity_pid_fixture_73d9e26b); then quiet_status=0; else quiet_status=$?; fi
if omitted=$(pidof -o "$child" parity_pid_fixture_73d9e26b); then omit_status=0; else omit_status=$?; fi
printf 'release\n' > gate
wait "$child"
[[ $handshake == ready && $found == 0 && $out == "$child" ]]
[[ $single == 0 && $one == "$child" && $quiet_status == 0 && -z $quiet ]]
[[ $omit_status == 1 && -z $omitted ]]
printf 'owned child matched; quiet and omission correct\n'
